package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain code that executes arbitrary code at install/import time, downloads and runs remote payloads, steals sensitive information (credentials, crypto wallets), establishes remote access, evades analysis, and/or exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Many use obfuscation, anti-VM checks, and polymorphic payloads to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executes code from a remote server at install time, which is not expected for legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only handle package installation, not execute remote code.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py or install scripts executing network requests or shell commands
Base64-encoded or obfuscated code in install-time scripts
Clipboard monitoring and replacement for crypto wallet patterns
Anti-VM or anti-analysis checks in install/runtime code
PowerShell or curl/wget invocation from Python install scripts
Discord webhook or API usage for exfiltration
file_indicators: setup.py containing exec(urlopen(...)) or similar patterns
Temporary files created and executed during install
Presence of slack-helper, WindowsCache.exe, update.exe, or similar dropped binaries
Obfuscated or whitespace-hidden code in setup.py
network_indicators: Requests to Dropbox URLs for executable downloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python package installation events that trigger network requests, process execution, or PowerShell/shell commands. Flag setup.py or install scripts containing obfuscated, encoded, or remote code execution logic. Detect clipboard manipulation for crypto wallet patterns. Watch for connections to known C2 infrastructure, Discord webhooks, or suspicious cloud storage URLs. Use static analysis to identify anti-VM checks and dynamic analysis to catch runtime behaviors.
